title: Connection-stability simulator for streaming chat completions
creator: Maya R. Singh
description: Build a connection-stability simulator that recreates realistic client behaviors for streaming chat/completions (SSE + WebSocket) at scale. The simulator focuses on connection churn, mid-stream reconnects, token-level pacing, backpressure, and multi-tenant mixing to detect regressions in tokens/sec and p95 tail latency. This ticket is the end-to-end harness: workload definition, runner service, dashboards, and automated regression detection hooks.
acceptance_criteria: Simulator can sustain 50k concurrent logical streams (configurable) across SSE and WSS endpoints with realistic churn profiles
Measures and emits per-request and aggregated metrics: tokens/sec, p50/p90/p95/p99 latency for first token and tail, bytes/sec, reconnect frequency
Provides synthetic user profiles (bursting, slow-consumers, long-lived, frequent reconnects) selectable via config
Integration tests that reproduce a known baseline (controlled run) and an injected regression that increases p95 by >=20%
Regression detector alerts (Slack + PagerDuty test route) on statistically significant drift using the configured control-chart + EWMA rules
Dashboard in Console showing live tokens/sec, connection churn, per-model p95 drift with historical baselines and cohort comparison
Runbook that describes how to triage common failure modes (proxy hotspots, KV cache cold starts, admission throttling)
implementation_notes: Generator implemented in Rust (tokio) for lightweight per-connection state and deterministic token pacing
Use a horizontal pool of worker VMs with k8s HPA to reach target concurrency; each worker maintains thousands of logical streams via multiplexed sockets
Connection profiles: steady, bursty, slow-consumer (low read rate), intermittent reconnect (5-30s downtime), and long-tail chat sessions
Token injection follows real production token length distributions per model family; incorporate KV cache warm/cold trajectories to measure cache impact
Support running through our edge proxy and directly against runtime nodes to isolate proxy vs runtime regressions
Expose a control plane API to start/stop scenarios, change churn rates, and pin model variants for A/B runs
Persist raw trace samples (aggregated) to BigQuery for regression analysis; metrics emit to Prometheus + Console ingest
test_plan: Smoke: 100 concurrent streams SSE + WSS dual test with simple prompt set
Scale step test: 1k -> 10k -> 50k logical streams, measure tokens/sec and p95 at each step
Churn sweep: vary reconnect rate from 0.1%/min to 10%/min and observe tail behavior
KV cache experiment: run identical workload with cache enabled vs disabled to measure 95th percentile delta
Regression injection: introduce delayed kernel (simulated 50-150ms extra per-token) to validate detector sensitivity
Chaos run: induce partial network partition to emulate AZ-level proxy degradation and verify graceful fallback policies
metrics_and_alerting: Per-request: first-token latency, last-token latency, tokens emitted, reconnects, bytes transferred
Aggregates: tokens/sec (global and per-model), p50/p90/p95/p99 for first/last token, connection churn rate
Regression detection: EWMA on p95 with control limits; trigger on sustained >15% increase over hourly baseline or 25% over 24h
Alerts: Slack channel #perf-regressions (informational), PagerDuty on production-affecting sustained regression (>30% p95 uplift + customer impact high)
Dashboards: Console -> runtime-performance -> Streaming Stability with cohort selector and baseline overlay
